description: Der Markt Mainleus plant förderfähige Bereiche seines Gemeindegebiets mit Glasfaser bis ins Haus im Rahmen des Betreibermodells zu erschließen. Das geplante Erschließungsge-biet enthält 472 Adressen, die Baukosten wurden in LPH 3 ermittelt und umfassen ca. 3,19 Mio. EUR netto bzw. 3,79 Mio. EUR brutto (ohne Planungsleistungen). Grundlage für die Bearbeitung ist der FTTB-Masterplan von 2018 mit dem kompletten Markt-gemeindegebiet (Anlage 01_LB) und das mittels BayGibitR geförderte Erschließungsgebiet (Anlage 02_LB). Als Betreiber konnte die Telekom D GmbH gewonnen werden. Es wurden die Trassen auf öffentlichem Grund, inkl. Aufnahme der jeweiligen Oberflächen und unter Berücksichtigung vorhandener Leitungen (Trassenauskunft TK, Energieversorger usw.) aufgenommen und stehen als Shape-Elemente zur Verfügung. Es wurde eine offene Bauweise geplant. Inwieweit auch Pressungen oder Spülbohrungen zum Einsatz kommen/sollen/müssen, bleibt dem folgenden Planungsschritt vorbehalten. Für die benötigten Netzverteiler (=Übergabepunkte an den Betreiber) wurden Standortvorschläge erarbeitet und mit dem Markt Mainleus abgestimmt (Standortsicherung ist abgeschlossen). Die Trassen auf privatem Grund wurden noch nicht geplant (da für den Förderantrag irrelevant). Genehmi-gungen und Gestattungen wurden noch nicht eingeholt, wobei der Markt Mainleus mit den geplanten Trassen auf kommunalem Grund grundsätzlich einverstanden ist. Grundsätzlich wird das Projekt nach Materialkonzept und GIS-Nebenbestimmungen des Bundes ge-plant/umgesetzt. Zu den vorgenannten aktuellen Informationen des Projektes werden somit – neben dem Masterplan und dem Erschließungsgebiet – folgende Unterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt: - Detailpläne aus der Entwurfsplanung LPH 3 (Anlage 03_LB) - Trassenpläne aus der Entwurfsplanung LPH 3 (Anlage 04_LB) - Standortsicherungen für Netzbauten (Anlage 05_LB) - Datensatz (shp) des Masterplans (Anlage 06_LB) - Kostenprognose (Anlage 07_LB)

title: Ireland – Environmental training services – Provision of an Environmental Education Course
description: SKDP is seeking to deliver an environmental educational short course which is both informative and practical and which will be made available for participation to the public in the South Kerry area. This initiative is being developed in line with the 2023 – 2027 LEADER programme objectives which incorporates a number of thematic areas, one of which is ‘Sustainable Development and Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation’. A sub-theme under this core theme is ‘Climate Change Capacity Building’. Climate change presents an ever-growing and existential challenge to Kerry’s rich and biodiverse ecological habitats and overall environmental health. This challenge is one which will affect not only our natural flora and fauna but also the wellness and health of our communities as well as their economic resilience as Kerry’s economy is heavily reliant on tourism. The Kerry Local Development Strategy which was developed through public participation to inform the core objectives of this current iteration of LEADER, found that an understanding of the science of climate change and in particular how Ireland and Southwest Ireland will be affected was a noticeable knowledge gap when engaging with the local communities. Priorities identified under the current LEADER programme include the provision of environmental educational training resources. To identify the specific areas of environmental education which groups would be most interested in, SKDP undertook a short public survey which was widely distributed to communities and community groups and remained open for 4.5 weeks. SKDP received 49 responses, with the outcome directing this RFT. SKDP are now seeking to enlist the expertise of an experienced environmental education/ training provider to develop and deliver an environmental education course. It is envisaged that this course will support the needs and priorities of these groups and their communities and support them to take meaningful local action for the environment. The objective of this RFT is to seek tenders from environmental education / training providers for the delivery of an environmental education course which will support communities to take meaningful local action to support biodiversity and to increase the resilience of habitats in their local areas. The course should be delivered as three modules. This is to enable participants, if they are unable to complete the full course, to complete one or two modules. The modules are as follows: 1. title: COPPER PILLAR FLIP CHIP ASSEMBLY TECHNOLOGY FOR HIGH DENSITY COMPONENTS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop flip chip assembly capabilities for <15nm technology nodes and the bumping process for microbumps and/or copper pillars at wafer level.Description: This activity is aimed at the capabilities development within Europe of copper pillars and/or microbumps flip-chip assembly, that could further enable the next level of integration of SiP, which is 2.5D and 3D. Standard solder flip chip bumps are not capable to meet the high density level of advanced technology nodes <15nm and its reduced dimensions. For those technology nodes only microbumps and/or copper pillars are the most recognized and reliable assembly methods. The activity aims at developing both the copper pillars wafer bumping technology and the flip chip assembly capabilities onto a silicon substrate.The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Selection of the microbumps technology to be developed - Microbump wafer bumping development - Flip-chip assembly onto silicon substrate - Initial process characterization and definition of process key parameters.The expected deliverables of the activity include: - Breadboard demonstrator of the assembly capabilities - Initial characterization of the process performance (e.g. yield, failure modes, etc). The next steps of this activity will be the flip-chip assembly ontoasilicon interposer and/or another die, thus enabling 3D integration.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl.
